kuru.notes: MN 82 opens in Kuru country. The MN 81 citation shares a page with MN 82. The packet misses kurūnaṁ in the sixteen-country lists in AN 3.70, 8.42, 8.43 and 8.45. In each, Sujato names Kuru one segment before the Pali list.

kusinārā.notes: MN 103:1.2 has pisinārāyaṁ where Sujato and DPPN give Kusinārā, explaining its absence from the packet. MN 102 and AN 4.74–75 are adjacent citation hits. AN 3.132:4.1 is a chapter summary. Check the entry’s identification of the birth pilgrimage site as Kapilavatthu. DN 16:5.8 describes the site by the event, and Snp 3.11:5.3 places the birth at Lumbinī.

kāla.notes: Cāpā addresses her husband in Thig 13.3. The candidate instead describes the paccekabuddha named alongside Upakāḷa in MN 116:6.9. The Pali pair Kāḷūpakāḷā has its own dictionary line, so the packet lists only the husband’s verses.

kālaka.notes: AN 4.24 names the Sāketa monastery associated with the DPD donor. The candidate concerns a monk in AN 10.87 and questions whether Kāḷaka is a name at all. At 1.1 the app’s Pali reads kālaṅkataṁ bhikkhuṁ (a monk who had died), while Sujato calls the monk Kalandaka. Neither reading establishes a monk named Kāḷaka. AN 10.86 is an adjacent citation hit.

kālakhemaka.notes: The Sakyan’s lodge appears in MN 122:2.2. MN 121 is an adjacent citation hit.

kālakārāma.notes: AN 4.24 opens at the monastery in Sāketa. The citation also lands in AN 4.23.

kālasilā.notes: DPD points to MN 13. The Jain ascetics at the Black Rock on Isigili appear in MN 14:15.2. The Saṁyutta episodes are SN 4.23, 8.10 and 22.87. The page matches also include SN 4.22, 8.9 and 22.88.

kāligodhā.notes: SN 55.39 names the Sakyan woman. AN 1.193 and the attribution of Thag 16.7 name Bhaddiya’s mother. Ud 2.10:1.3 gives the same relationship with the spelling Kāḷīgodhā, which has a separate DPD lemma. SN 55.38 and the AN groups on either side of AN 1.188–197 are adjacent citation hits.

kālī.notes: AN 1.267 and AN 10.26 both call the laywoman kuraragharikā. AN 1.248–257 and 1.268–277 are page overlaps. Thig 5.6:6.1 attributes the verses to Mittā Kāḷī Therī, for whom the packet supplies no entry. Thag 2.16:1 describes the woman handling bones in Mahākāḷa’s verses, exactly the episode in Kāḷī 05. Sujato reads kāḷī as a description of her complexion, so the packet misses her.

kāmabhū.notes: Kāmabhū meets Ānanda in SN 35.233 and Citta in SN 41.5 and 41.6. The citation list picks up SN 35.232 and 41.4 and misses the second Citta discourse. SN 35.237 and 41.10 name Kāmabhū in chapter summaries.

kāmada.notes: The deity speaks in SN 2.6. The neighboring citations concern Dāmali (SN 2.5), Pañcālacaṇḍa (SN 2.7) and Tāyana (SN 2.8).

kāmaṇḍā.notes: Udāyī is in Todeyya’s mango grove at Kāmaṇḍā in SN 35.133:1.1. SN 35.132 takes place at Makkarakaṭa.

kāraṇapālī.notes: The Licchavis’ superintendent speaks with Piṅgiyānī in AN 5.194. AN 5.193 concerns Saṅgārava, and the mention in AN 5.200:7.2 is a chapter summary.

kāsi.notes: DN 19:36.9 distinguishes Bārāṇasī from the Kāsi people whose capital it is. MN 26:25.19 calls the destination kāsinaṁ puraṁ (the city of the Kāsis) and MN 26:26.1 names it Bārāṇasī. DPPN’s identification of Phussa’s birthplace (Kāsi 02) with that city is conjectural. The verb in mā kāsi (‘do not do’) produced the false mention in Thig 12.1:9.3. The packet misses the kingdom lists in AN 3.70, 8.42, 8.43 and 8.45, where the Pali and English fall in different segments. AN 10.28 is a page overlap with AN 10.29.

kātiyāna.notes: Thag 6.7 addresses the elder and attributes the verses to him. SN 2.30:8.1 names Pakudhaka Kātiyāna among the other teachers. Showing the elder’s biography for that occurrence would misidentify him.

kātiyānī.notes: AN 1.265 names Kātiyānī for her unwavering confidence. The citation also lands in the AN groups 1.248–257 and 1.268–277.

kūṭāgārasālā.notes: Despite the empty mention list, MN 36:1.2 and AN 8.53:1.1 both read vesāliyaṁ … mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ. Sujato translates the name as ‘the hall with the peaked roof’. Many page hits are neighboring texts. For example, MN 35 opens at the hall, SN 35.124 sets Ugga there, and SN 55.30 sets Nandaka there. MN 34, SN 35.125 and SN 55.28–29 do not supply those settings.

lakkhaṇa.notes: The packet misses the monk because Sujato translates his name as ‘Mark’. SN 19.1:1.3 names both Lakkhaṇa and Mahāmoggallāna on Gijjhakūṭa, and Lakkhaṇa asks why his companion smiled. SN 18.22 is an adjacent citation hit.

lohicca.notes: DPD cites DN 12, where Lohicca lives at Sālavatikā and questions the Buddha. In SN 35.132, Lohicca’s pupils visit Mahākaccāna at Makkarakaṭa. SN 35.133:8.4 recites the preceding discourse title in the chapter summary. The episode in SN 35.133 concerns Udāyī and the Verahaccāni brahmin woman.

macchikāsaṇḍa.notes: DPD calls Macchikāsaṇḍa a forest. Its example SN 41.4:1.1 distinguishes the locality Macchikāsaṇḍa from the grove Ambāṭakavana where the elders stay, in agreement with the DPPN township entry. SN 40.11 is an adjacent citation hit.

maddakucchi.notes: SN 1.38 and SN 4.13 place the wounded Buddha at the deer park. SN 1.37 and SN 4.12 are adjacent citation hits. DPPN also relates Māra’s visit to DN 16. At DN 16:3.42–43 the Buddha recalls his words to Ānanda at the park. The encounter with Māra during his injury is in SN 4.13.
